title: A conormal surjection detects unramifiedness along a common closed subscheme
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed immersions with $f\circ i=j$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $\mathcal I_i$ and $\mathcal I_j$ be their ideal sheaves [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and put $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=i^*\mathcal I_i$ and $\mathcal C_{Z/Y}=j^*\mathcal I_j$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Suppose that the canonical conormal morphism $\mathcal C_{Z/Y}\to\mathcal C_{Z/X}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-functorial], for the square with bottom map $f$ and top map $1_Z$, is surjective as a map of sheaves of modules. Then for every $z\in Z$ there is an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X$ of $i(z)$ such that $f|_W:W\to Y$ is unramified [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-unramified-morphism].

source.place: Tags 067L (morphisms-lemma-two-immersions), its right-exact conormal sequence, and 02GF (morphisms-lemma-unramified-at-point), equivalence of unramifiedness and vanishing of the cotangent fibre; also 01R4 (morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial) for the specified arrow.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-two-closed-immersions-conormal-exact] to the given $f,i,j$. Its hypotheses are precisely that both immersions are closed and $f\circ i=j$, so they hold without extra finiteness assumptions. It supplies the right-exact sequence $\mathcal C_{Z/Y}\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal C_{Z/X}\xrightarrow{v}i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y}\to0$. The statement of that node specifies that $u$ is the very conormal morphism assumed surjective in this item, with top map $1_Z$ and bottom map $f$.

source.place: Tag 067L (morphisms-lemma-two-immersions), sequence and specified first arrow.

proof.text: In the right-exact sequence from step 1, $vu=0$ and $u$ is surjective, so $v=0$: locally lift any section of $\mathcal C_{Z/X}$ through $u$ and apply $v$. Since $v$ is also surjective, every section of $i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y}$ is locally zero and hence is zero by the sheaf axiom. Therefore $i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y}=0$. This is the elementary cokernel calculation; no exactness after a nonflat tensor product is being asserted.

source.place: Tag 067L (morphisms-lemma-two-immersions), elementary consequence of its right-exact sequence.

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$ and put $x=i(z)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ and $M=\Omega^1_{X/Y,x}$. The pullback-stalk isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] identifies the zero stalk from step 2 with $M\otimes_A B$. Tensoring this zero module with $\kappa(z)$ over $B$ and associating tensors gives $M\otimes_A\kappa(z)=0$; on pure tensors the identification is $(m\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto m\otimes bc$, with inverse $m\otimes c\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes c$. The closed-immersion definition [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $A\to B$ surjective: the homeomorphism onto its image identifies $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x$ with $B$, and the structure-sheaf surjection lifts each germ. It is a local map because $i$ is a scheme morphism. Thus $B=A/K$ for a proper ideal $K\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ and its unique maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_A/K$. The residue-field definition [def-weil-residue-field] identifies the induced map $\kappa(x)=A/\mathfrak m_A\to\kappa(z)\cong(A/K)/(\mathfrak m_A/K)$ with $[a]\mapsto[[a]]$. This is an $A$-algebra isomorphism, with inverse $[[a]]\mapsto[a]$; the quotient relations make both maps well defined. Tensoring its inverse with $M$ therefore gives $M\otimes_A\kappa(x)=0$. All tensors here are the scalar extensions of [def-weil-module-base-change].

source.place: Tag 02GF (morphisms-lemma-unramified-at-point), cotangent fibre in (5); pullback stalk calculation: sheaves.tex Tag 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules).

proof.text: Apply (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of [lem-sfb-unramified-cotangent-fibre-criterion] to $f$ and $x=i(z)$. The assumed local finite type of $f$ is exactly its finiteness hypothesis, and step 3 gives its zero cotangent-fibre hypothesis. It produces an open $W\subseteq X$ containing $i(z)$ with $f|_W$ unramified over the original target $Y$. Since $z$ was arbitrary, this proves the stated assertion at every point of $Z$. If $Z$ is empty there is no point to choose and the conclusion is vacuous.
